On the 12-hour baseline it is a $2.29 fall per HYPE, and on the t0 mid a $2.99 rise.

70.9 Findings

As expected.

  • The flow after the run separates the patterns, and the measures taken inside the run read the same across them.

    The median event that holds takes another $0.43m of net taker volume in the surge direction over [t1, t1 + 15 min), and the median event that reverts meets $3.16m of net taker volume against it, which as a fraction of the run's own surge-side volume is +0.03 against -0.23. The rank test is H = 129.7 at p = 6.7e-29 on 492 events and the Spearman against rho_15 is +0.56.

  • The size of the surge separates gated events from small price moves and reads the same across the gated patterns.

    The median surge-side volume is $15.0m on the events that hold, $17.6m on the partly reverted, $15.2m on the reverted and $8.5m on the small price moves, with a rank test of p = 0.29 across the three gated patterns.

  • The population's unwind tilt is the same on every pattern.

    +1.09 bps on the events that hold, +1.46 partly reverted, +0.74 reverted, against an interquartile range of 5.7 bps and a rank test of p = 0.90 on 442 events. The +1.55 bps of section 64.3 holds across all of them.

  • Executions move about three quarters of the surge-side quote's travel away from the mid in every pattern.

    The share is 0.756 on the events that hold and 0.784 on those that revert (p = 0.28), and cancels move 4% in every pattern (p = 0.82). The execution share of section 64.6 is the same whatever the price does afterwards.

  • The surge-side quote ends the 15 minutes after the run nearer the mid on the events that revert.

    Travel back toward the mid over travel away is 0.968 on the events that hold, 1.041 partly reverted and 1.101 reverted, H = 216.0 at p = 1.2e-47 on 492 events, the strongest ordering of any separator here. Both directions carry more travel on the events that revert, 1,437 bps away against 1,168.

  • Only the flow after the run survives the multivariate fit.

    In the standardized ordinary least squares of rho_15, the flow after the run carries +0.113 per standard deviation with an HC3 standard error of 0.032, and the other five terms are within 1.0 standard error of zero. R-squared is 0.149 on 439 events.

  • A longer baseline makes every peak move larger and the retention ratio higher, and the classification mostly survives it.

    The median gated peak move is 260 bps on the t0 mid and 410 bps on the 12-hour median mid, and 384 of 492 gated events keep their pattern when rho_15 is re-anchored on the 2-hour median mid.

Not as expected (possible design cause).

  • On the minute snapshot the accumulation tilt orders the wrong way, and that snapshot is stale in this phase.

    The snapshot tilt against the market maker's own prior 2 hours is -13.6 bps on the events that hold and -18.0 on the events that revert, so the population would quote further from the exit on the events whose price comes back. Possible design cause: a reverting event is the one where the price ran furthest fastest, which drags a stale resting order's distance to the mid without the market maker having moved it. The placement-time measure supports that cause: over all rows it reads the accumulation tilt at +0.9 bps against -19.8 bps on the snapshot (drafts/place0922_section.md). Check: split the placement-time tilt by price pattern on the same 492 events. Section 64.11 carries this as D9.

  • The reverted events draw fewer accumulating market makers and a smaller share of the surge.

    5 accumulating market makers at the median against 7 on the events that hold, absorbing 7.2% of the surge's taker USD against 13.5%. Possible design cause: the reverted events are the shortest and fastest, 9.5 minutes from t0 to the price extreme against 25 on the events that hold, and the population rule needs an inventory excursion measured over minutes to flag a market maker at all. Check: recompute the population share on a duration-matched subsample, or per minute of run length.

  • The time from the run's start to the price extreme orders with the pattern nearly as strongly as the flow does.

    It is 25 minutes on the events that hold, 16.5 on the partly reverted and 9.5 on the reverted, H = 95.7 at p = 1.7e-21, against H = 129.7 for the flow. This is a property of the outcome window: the peak and the 15-minute endpoint are both searched inside the same look-ahead, so an event whose extreme arrives early has more of the window left in which to lose the move. Check: recompute rho_15 on a fixed 30-minute horizon from t_pp in place of t1 and see whether the ordering survives.

70.10 Validation

Every check in tables/rev0922_validation.csv passes unless noted
  • 922 events = 492 gated + 428 small price move + 2 against, and the gated split reproduces the published split exactly (project record, section 41.4): 206 held, 224 partly reverted, 62 reverted. The gated flag equals big_move_full on every event.
  • All 351 dates are kept, with three events on 2025-10-10 and three on 2026-01-31.
  • The surge-side taker USD computed here reproduces the catalogue's own hit_usd_1m to 2.3e-16 relative on all 922 events, and the run's minute count equals length_min_1m on all 922.
  • The four travel shares sum to 1 on all 910 events with travel in the run, to 2.2e-16.
  • Coverage on the 492 gated events, stated per separator in the validation table: flow and the peak-excursion measures 492 of 492; the book measures 490 in the run, because two events are one-minute runs whose build window is empty, and 492 after it; spread and depth 490; the market-maker measures 433 to 478, the shortfall being 14 gated events with no accumulating market maker and a further 25 to 45 whose market makers lack a resting order on one side in the accumulation or the unwind window. No event is dropped silently: every quantile cell in every table carries its own n.
  • The accumulating population is 6,173 of the 118,269 (event, market maker) rows of tables/redef2_pop_event_mm_F1.csv, spread over 849 of the 922 events, the same cut that section 64.3 reports. Resting size is zero on both sides in the PRE2H window on 8.2% of those rows, because this population file predates the 2026-09-15 order-store fix (tables/POPULATION_OF_RECORD.md), which is why the exit-side size share carries a smaller n than the distances.

70.11 What this does not establish

  • rho_15 is a 15-minute look-ahead, and the three strongest separators are measured over the same 15 minutes.

    The net taker flow after the run and the price path it is compared against occupy the same window, so the two move together by construction as much as by mechanism, and nothing here says the flow arrived first. The quote's travel back over its travel away is stronger still and carries less information: it is read off the same best-quote series whose midpoint defines rho_15, so it restates the outcome in book units. The minutes from t0 to the price extreme are a property of the same window.

  • The tilt is a minute-snapshot measure.

    q_ACC_* and q_UNW_* read the distance from each resting order to the minute's mid on a 1-minute grid, so they record where orders sat during the minute. The placement-time measure of drafts/place0922_section.md agrees with the snapshot in the unwind, +0.35 against +0.49 bps, and contradicts it in accumulation, +0.9 against -19.8 bps, which is why the accumulation rows are folded.

  • With 32 separators tested, 4 clear the Bonferroni threshold of 0.0016.

    They are the two flow measures after the run, the quote's back-over-away ratio after the run and the time to the price extreme. The spread ratio at 0.054, the accumulation tilt at 0.060 and the market-maker count at 0.055 are readings a single pre-registered test would have called, and no test here was pre-registered.

  • The ordinary least squares is descriptive.

    Its terms are contemporaneous with each other and with the outcome, the dollar terms are right-skewed and standardizing them does not fix that, and 53 of the 492 gated events are dropped for a missing input. No coefficient identifies an effect.

  • The book measures cover the surge side only.

    The opposite side's quote travel is not measured here, so the section cannot say whether the far side's quotes moved differently on the events that revert; the other-side depth ratio of Table 31 is a 1-minute resting-size measure, not a tick measure.

  • ts_bookdiff_lt and _le are a reconstruction.

    Their timestamp tie-break is not HyperCore's documented action ordering, and a book update carrying a fill and a placement at the same microsecond cannot be split, so the trade and cancel attribution is a lower bound on how mixed the book updates are.

71. Liquidation cascades as time episodes

HYPE has 301 liquidation episodes above $1m of liquidated notional over 2025-04-01 to 2026-06-30, and 187 of them, 62.1%, share at least one minute with an event in the one-sided surge catalogue or the net-flow box catalogue. At the 15-minute gap rule the flow catalogues therefore reach most cascades.

  • 62.1% clears the coverage rule's 60% bar, narrowly and only from 15 minutes upward. Under a 5-minute gap the share is 57.1%.
  • Coverage is stronger in dollars than in episodes, because the caught episodes are the large ones. They hold $1,383.7m of the $1,624.4m that the 301 episodes liquidate, 85.2%.
  • The two definitions agree completely at the top. All 47 one-sided surges labeled a liquidation cascade contain an episode, and 45 of them contain one above the $1m floor.
  • These counts read each net-flow box on a window shorter than the box. With each box on its full window a recheck puts coverage at 67.1% at the 15-minute gap and 67.2% at 5 minutes (D10 in section 64.11).
Setup: populations, sources and compute

The liquidation stream. Every HYPE trade in data_enriched/hype/grouped_trade_oid/{date}.parquet with dir_bucket == 'liquidation', over the 456 daily partitions from 2025-04-01 to 2026-06-30: 101,590 trades, $1,965.2m of liquidated notional, 48,961 distinct victim wallets, on 435 of the 456 dates. dir_bucket is assigned in the priority adl > liquidation > open > reversal > close, and liquidated_volume > 0 is set only where the fill's liquidatedUser == user, so this bucket is exactly the victim side of a liquidation that was not auto-deleveraged. The 6,230 ADL trades on the same dates, $189.9m, are excluded, as docs/conventions.md requires. Both maker and taker roles are kept: 21.1% of the liquidated notional fills maker-side, so a crossed == true filter would drop a fifth of the stream and drop it unevenly across episodes.

The flow catalogues. The 922 one-sided taker surges, tables/redef4_events_F1_one_sided.csv, and the 915 net-flow boxes, tables/redef2_imb_events_recommended_absgate.csv, each with its window [t0, t1). Four one-sided surges fall on 2025-03-30 and 2025-03-31, before the episode window opens; three carry the no-big-price-move class and one the big-price-move class.

Reused. The extraction contract, meaning the source table, the column list and the victim definition, comes from Allium/experiments/leverage/code/build_liq_trades_sidecar.py. The gap-run episode labeling comes from Allium/experiments/leverage/leverage_cohort/wrapup_2026-09-06/code/build_cascade_episodes.py, with its per-coin partition dropped because this stream is one coin. The Allium sidecar file itself starts on 2025-09-27 and covers only the last nine months of this window, so the extraction is rerun on HYPE alone against the same source partitions.

Builder. code/casc0922_episodes.py, run 2026-09-22 inside the interactive allocation, 16 reader threads, 16 seconds wall. Outputs tables/casc0922_episodes.csv, _summary.csv, _top10.csv, _overlap_f1.csv, _f1_by_class.csv, _caught_vs_missed.csv, _monthly.csv and figures/redefinition/casc0922_episodes_timeline.png.

Every exhibit includes 2025-10-10 and 2026-01-31. No date is excluded anywhere in this section.

71.1 Two definitions of a cascade, side by side

The project uses the word cascade for two different objects: a class label on an event a flow rule already selected, and a run of liquidation trades that is an event in its own right.

The class label. A property of an event that is already in a flow catalogue. An event is labeled a liquidation cascade when forced taker USD inside its window is at least a tenth of all taker USD in that window:

forced_share = (liquidation USD + ADL USD taken inside the window) / taker USD inside the window
liq_cascade  = forced_share >= 0.10

It holds for 47 of the 922 one-sided surges and 41 of the 915 net-flow boxes. It can only label surges the flow rules already selected.

The time episode. An event in its own right, selected on liquidations. Order the victim-side HYPE liquidation trades by timestamp and cut the sequence wherever consecutive trades sit more than g minutes apart. Each maximal run is one episode:

episode boundary at trade i  <=>  t(i) - t(i-1) > g minutes
g = 15 minutes for the headline, with g = 5, 30 and 60 as sensitivity

Per episode: the first and last liquidation timestamp, the elapsed minutes between them, the summed liquidated notional and HYPE size, the count of distinct victim wallets, the count of liquidation trades, and the dominant side. The dominant side is forced_sell when victims with long positions supply the larger share of the liquidated notional and forced_buy otherwise.

The floor. An episode enters the coverage population when its liquidated notional is at least $1m. At the 15-minute gap the floor keeps 301 of 4,159 episodes and 82.7% of the liquidated notional; the median episode below it liquidates $10.9k across three wallets.

Overlap. An episode and a flow event overlap when they share a minute.

  • The episode's minutes run from its first to its last liquidation minute, both included.
  • A one-sided surge enters with the minutes of its run [t0, t1).
  • A net-flow box enters with the minutes from its start to the start of its last 30-minute bin, so a one-bin box enters as its first minute. Section 64.11 carries the rerun on the full box window as D10.
  • gap_to_nearest_flow_min is the minute distance from an episode to the closest event of either catalogue, and is 0 where they overlap.
  • Overlap is a timing statement and carries no claim that the liquidations caused the surge.

Set-up problem. Each net-flow box enters the overlap test as its first minute when it has one 30-minute bin, 767 of the 915, because the build reads the start of the last bin as the last minute. It should enter as [t0, t1); a recheck puts above-floor coverage at 67.1% at the 15-minute gap and 67.2% at 5 minutes (D10).

The $1m floor decides which liquidation runs count as cascades, and the gap rule barely moves that set. Coverage of the above-floor episodes rises with the gap.

  • The floor decides which episodes are cascades, and the gap rule barely moves that set.

    The episode count falls from 6,316 at the 5-minute gap to 2,104 at 60, while the count above the $1m floor stays between 262 and 301. Runs that merge under a wider gap were already large enough to clear the floor separately.

  • Coverage rises with the gap, and the verdict turns on it.

    The share of above-floor episodes overlapping a flow event runs 57.1%, 62.1%, 69.9% and 81.3% across the four gap rules, so the 60% bar is met at 15, 30 and 60 minutes and missed at 5.

  • Dollar coverage is 23 points higher than episode coverage.

    At the 15-minute gap the caught episodes are 62.1% of the count and 85.2% of the notional, so the episodes the catalogues reach are the large ones.

  • Both catalogues are needed and the surge catalogue does most of the work.

    Of the 301 above-floor episodes, 86 overlap both catalogues, 86 a one-sided surge alone, 15 a net-flow box alone and 114 neither. The 86 that overlap both hold $1,100.9m, two thirds of the population's notional.

  • The class label and the episode definition agree on every cascade.

    All 47 contain an episode and 45 contain one above the $1m floor (Table 40). The two events whose largest overlapping episode falls below the $1m floor are 2025-04-03 10:01, at $84k and a forced share of 4.0%, and 2025-05-09 04:53, at $884k and 13.7%.

  • A surge containing a liquidation usually contains a small one.

    57.8% of the no-big-price-move surges overlap an episode, and the median largest episode inside one liquidates $3.7k. Restricting to the $1m floor drops the share to 9.1%, so the 10% forced-share label separates the classes the way it is meant to.

    The other 29 overlap an episode that starts before the surge window or runs past its end, so the surge window and the liquidation run are not the same interval even where both fire.

Figure 9. HYPE liquidation episodes and flow-catalogue coverage, 15-minute gap rule.

What one mark is, and what the figure excludes

One mark per episode at the 15-minute gap rule, positioned at its first liquidation timestamp, with the summed liquidated notional on a logarithmic vertical axis. Every mark below the floor takes no part in the coverage statistic. The axis is clipped at $1k, which hides 1,056 of the 4,159 episodes; 93% of them liquidate one or two wallets and the largest holds 14. The band below the floor thins over 2025-04 to 2025-06 and again in 2026-03 and 2026-04, where a month holds 166 to 232 episodes against 300 to 381 in the busiest months.

Episodes above the floor arrive in every month of the window, and the misses sit at the bottom of the above-floor band throughout it, so the coverage gap follows episode size and holds in every period.

71.6 Findings

As expected.

  • The flow catalogues reach 62.1% of the above-floor episodes and 85.2% of their notional.

    That clears the coverage rule's 60% bar, with 114 episodes standing outside both catalogues.

  • Coverage rises with the gap rule.

    It runs 57.1% to 81.3% from 5 to 60 minutes, because a wider gap merges fragments into longer episodes that are more likely to touch a flow window.

  • The class label and the time episode agree at the top.

    All 47 one-sided surges labeled a liquidation cascade contain an episode, and 9 of the 10 largest episodes carry that label.

  • Long victims dominate 228 of the 301 above-floor episodes.

    Of the 10 largest, 9 are forced sells, which matches a market whose liquidations cluster on down moves.

Not as expected (possible design cause).

  • The verdict flips with the gap rule.

    57.1% at 5 minutes fails the 60% bar that 62.1% at 15 minutes passes. Possible design cause: the one-sided surge catalogue anchors on a 1-minute onset inside a 30-minute box and so selects short concentrated surges, while a 5-minute gap splits one liquidation run into fragments whose outer pieces fall outside that window. Check: recompute coverage with the episode interval padded by 5 and 10 minutes on each side, at every gap rule, and report how much of the 5-minute shortfall the padding recovers. A second cause is the box window of D10: with each box on its full window [t0, t1), a recheck puts the 5-minute coverage at 67.2%. Section 64.11 carries this as D8.

  • 75 of the 114 missed episodes stand more than 30 minutes from any flow event.

    The distance to the nearest one-sided surge or net-flow box reaches 962 minutes at p95 across the missed group. Possible design cause: these episodes liquidate a median $1.61m over 20.7 minutes, spread thinly enough that the minute-level taker flow never crosses the catalogues' entry bar. Check: read the 1-minute taker net and gross USD inside the 75 episode windows and compare them to the enter_bar_usd_1m of the surrounding 6 hours, then report how many sit below it.

  • The largest cascade is the least taker-driven.

    2025-10-10 20:52 fills 77.9% of its $527.8m maker-side, against 97% to 100% taker for the other 9 in the top 10. Possible design cause: the forced share that defines the class label counts taker USD only, so the largest liquidation event in the sample contributes just $116.4m to it. Check: recompute forced_share on liquidated notional including maker-side fills and report how many additional one-sided surges cross the 10% bar. Section 64.11 carries this as D7.

  • 51 of the 561 quiet surges hold an episode above the $1m floor.

    That is 9.1% of the no-big-price-move class, against 25.5% of the big-price-move class. Possible design cause: the class label reads forced share against the window's total taker USD, so a $1m liquidation inside a heavy voluntary surge stays under 10%. Check: report the forced share of those 51 events and how many sit between 5% and 10%.

71.7 Validation

What was checked
  • Episode keys are unique. episode_id has 6,316, 4,159, 3,062 and 2,104 distinct values against the same row counts at the 5, 15, 30 and 60-minute gaps.
  • Episode notional reconciles to the stream at every gap. Summed episode notional is $1,965,151,446.77 at all four gap rules against $1,965,151,446.77 of qualifying liquidation notional, a difference of $0.000003, and summed trade counts are 101,590 at each.
  • Date-file boundaries are merged, not cut. The stream is concatenated and sorted on timestamp before the runs are formed, and 13, 19, 34 and 61 episodes span a UTC date boundary at the four gap rules. All 456 daily partitions were read and none was missing.
  • The distance to the nearest flow event was checked against a brute-force scan. Recomputing f1_gap_to_nearest_min for 400 randomly drawn episodes by comparing each against all 922 surge windows reproduces the stored value on all 400.
  • Every month in the window carries episodes. At the 15-minute gap each of the 15 calendar months holds between 166 and 381 episodes and between 2 and 40 above the floor; the busiest by notional is 2025-10 at $646.8m and the lightest 2025-04 at $14.6m. Per-month rows are in tables/casc0922_monthly.csv.
  • The named dates are present. 2025-10-10 holds 18 episodes, 2 above the floor, $536.2m, both overlapping a flow event; 2026-01-31 holds 17 episodes, 4 above the floor, $11.1m, 3 overlapping.

71.8 What this does not establish

  • An episode is HYPE only.

    A wallet liquidated in HYPE and in three other coins in the same minute appears once here, and a cross-margin cascade that shows in BTC and reaches HYPE late is dated by its HYPE trades.

  • ADL is excluded, so an unwind resolved by auto-deleveraging leaves no episode.

    The 6,230 ADL trades in the window carry $189.9m, 8.8% of the combined forced notional.

  • Episode notional is the grouped trade's notional.

    liquidated_volume equals volume on 99.76% of victim rows; on the remaining 0.24% the grouped order was only partly liquidated and this section counts the whole trade.

  • The fill table is incomplete from 2025-04-01 to 2025-05-25.

    Maker and taker HYPE do not balance on those dates, which affects the taker share and the flow catalogues' entry bars there. 2025-04 and 2025-05 hold 6 of the 301 above-floor episodes, so the coverage statistic barely depends on them.

  • Overlap is a timing test.

    An episode and a surge that share one minute count as overlapping, whichever caused the other, and this section makes no claim about direction.

  • The $1m floor is a level, not a percentile.

    It selects 301 episodes at the 15-minute gap and 82.7% of the liquidated notional; a floor at $500k or $2m would move the coverage share, and that sensitivity is not computed here.
